who: John H. Zammito, historian of European intellectual history and science at Rice University; PhD Berkeley 1978.

evidence.says: Faculty entry on printed p. 667 names John H. Zammito, John Antony Weir Professor of History, with PhD University of California, Berkeley, 1978.
Rice identifies John Zammito as associate professor of history, already ten years at Rice in 1999, specializing in European intellectual history.
The candidate authority identifies John H. Zammito as Rice history professor emeritus and former John Antony Weir Professor; it also identifies his A Nice Derangement of Epistemes.

notes: The middle initial is an expanded form of the AHA name; the doctorate and Rice appointment agree.

who: Eric Zolov, historian of modern Latin America at Stony Brook University; PhD Chicago 1995.

evidence.says: The 2016 AHA profile identifies Zolov as Stony Brook associate professor, PhD Chicago 1995, working on twentieth-century Mexico and the global Cold War.
Stony Brook identifies Eric Zolov as professor of history, educated at Chicago, and author of Refried Elvis.
The candidate authority identifies the author of Refried Elvis and cites his 2016 Stony Brook faculty page as associate professor specializing in Latin America and the Cold War.

notes: The authority, university profile and AHA biography identify the same historian; affiliation, field and exact doctorate agree.

who: Charles K. Armstrong, historian of Korea and East Asia at Columbia University; PhD Chicago 1994.

who: Alison G. (Alison Gilbert) Olson, historian of early America and Anglo-American politics at Maryland, College Park; doctorate Oxford 1956.
